text:
The stock fell 1.79% today after surging nearly 16% over the past two weeks, likely pulling back as investors absorbed the escalating geopolitical risks in the Middle East. While tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure have driven crude oil prices higher (Brent at $125/barrel), Hurricane Isaias disrupting U.S. Gulf of Mexico production and threatening refineries created a mixed picture for a refiner — higher oil costs cut into margins even as refinery utilization sits near 93%.

The stock's sharp two-week rally appears to have been built on expectations that oil supply disruptions would benefit refiners through tighter markets and higher crack spreads (the profit margin between crude input and fuel output). Today's pullback may reflect profit-taking after such a large move, or renewed concern that refinery shutdowns from the hurricane could offset any margin benefits from elevated crude prices.
